answer_1.quote: We propose new approaches to add such additional constraints on the texts but at decoding time. ... we exploit a discriminator that is trained to determine if a text follows a given constraint or not; its output provides information to guide the generation toward texts that satisfy this expected constraint.
answer_1.outputs: generated reviews or sentences conditioned on a target class (e.g., positive/negative polarity, specific emotion)

answer_2.quote: We chose three different metrics to evaluate each of these aspects: 1) accuracy, which is verified by an external "oracle" discriminator ... 2) perplexity, which is computed using an "oracle" LM ... 3) Self‑BLEU score, which is the BLEU score of a sample using the other samples as references.

answer_4.quote: The evaluation has been performed on the CLS dataset by three volunteering colleagues, French native speakers. They labeled the same pool of reviews ... to give two scores for each review: 1. Polarity (1–5) ... 2. Readability (1–5) ...
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were asked to rate each generated review on polarity (how well it matches the desired label) and readability (how well it is written), both on a 1–5 scale.
